name: Aalto University Undergraduate Centre (Otaniemi main building)
features: Red-brick campus hall whose fan-shaped main auditorium rises like an outdoor amphitheatre over the square.

photos.file: File:Aalto University Undergraduate Centre, Otaniemi, Espoo (January 2020).jpg
File:Aalto University Undergraduate Centre, Otaniemi, Espoo (January 2017).jpg
File:Aalto University undergraduate centre on a sunny afternoon in June 2023.jpg

note: Built as the main building of the Helsinki University of Technology; Wikipedia's list of works dates it 1953–1967, the Aalto literature usually gives 1966.

name: Academic Bookstore (Kirjatalo)
features: Copper-clad bookshop whose three-storey hall is lit by crystal-like prismatic skylights.
note: Only two usable exterior photos: a 2007 street view and a 1969 black-and-white night view. The category also has a CC0 interior of the skylit hall (File:Bokhuset Helsingfors.jpg) if an interior is wanted.

name: Alvar Aalto Museum
features: White-tiled ribbed walls, a top-lit wavy exhibition hall and a small pool at the foot of the ridge.

name: Amos Rex
features: Underground galleries beneath Lasipalatsi square, lit by tiled domes with round skylights you can climb on.

name: Den Blå Planet (National Aquarium Denmark)
features: Whirlpool plan: aluminium-shingled arms curl out from a central foyer, with a pool at the entrance.

name: Copenhagen Police Headquarters (Politigården)
features: Severe Nordic-classical block on a triangular plan wrapped around a great round colonnaded courtyard.
note: Nordic Classicism (Wikipedia). Extras are Kampmann's own plan and watercolour, both public domain.

name: Enso-Gutzeit Headquarters (Stora Enso)
features: Carrara-marble grid of recessed windows on the harbour, sized to sit between the cathedral and the old town.

name: Filmhuset
features: Exposed-concrete film house shaped like a camera, its cast walls patterned like film strips.
note: Home of the Swedish Film Institute, Gärdet.

name: Henie Onstad Kunstsenter
features: Low concrete art centre stepping over a wooded headland on the Oslofjord.
note: At Høvikodden, about 10 km south-west of Oslo.

name: Holmenkollbakken ski jump
features: One continuous steel in-run cantilevered off the hill, wrapped in a mesh skin and lit at night over Oslo.
note: The jump was rebuilt to JDS's design for the 2011 World Ski Championships; earlier jumps stood on the site since 1892.

name: Moderna Museet Malmö
features: A 1901 brick power station extended with an orange-red annex clad in perforated metal.

name: Malmö Konsthall
features: One large flexible hall with a wooden floor under long glass roof lanterns, behind a plain street wall.
note: The two exterior photos are near-identical 2005 street views; the category also has good interior views of the top-lit hall.

name: Sanomatalo
features: Helsinki's first all-glass building: a newspaper house with public commercial floors at street level.

photos.file: File:Citizens' Square Helsinki Sanomatalo Pride Flags 2020-09-12.jpg

name: Seinäjoki City Hall
features: Council chamber clad in dark-blue tiles, reached by grass-and-timber steps climbing the slope.
note: Part of the Aalto Centre with the church, library, theatre and state offices; the original building dates 1959–1965 (annex 1973–74).

name: Sibelius Hall
features: Glulam timber concert hall in a glass box, joined to an old brick factory on the shore of Lake Vesijärvi.

name: Søholm Row Houses
features: Staggered yellow-brick row houses with mono-pitched roofs and high clerestory windows.
note: Søholm I (1946–1950) was the first phase; Jacobsen lived in one of its houses. Photo 3 shows the later Søholm II row.

name: Stegastein Viewpoint
features: A 30 m pine-and-steel walkway that leaps out from the hillside and stops in mid-air over the Aurlandsfjord.
note: Part of the Norwegian Scenic Routes programme. Year from the architects' published date (2006); Wikipedia gives no year.

name: Stockholm City Hall
features: Dark-red brick palace on the water with a 106 m tower, open courtyard and arcade to the lake.

photos.file: File:00 5245 Stockholm - Central Bridge, Town Hall tower.jpg

note: National Romanticism, the starting point of Nordic modern architecture; photos are in Category:Exterior of Stockholm City Hall.

name: Viikki Church
features: Almost all timber: spruce frame and interior, double-shingled aspen walls above a dry-stone base.

photos.file: File:Viikki Church in Latokartano, Viikki, Helsinki, Finland, 2022 July - 2.jpg

name: Härlanda Church
features: Heavy brick church and parish buildings round a lawn, with a free-standing brick bell tower.

photos.file: File:Härlanda Kyrka med klockstapel, Gothenburg, Sweden.jpg

note: No English Wikipedia article; the church is listed in the Peter Celsing article. Photos are 1300 px wide (CC BY 4.0).

name: Universeum
features: Science centre and aquarium built down a rocky slope, its glass and timber halls stepping with the hill.
note: The two usable exterior photos both show the street side with Liseberg behind; the category has few building views.

name: Helsinki Olympic Stadium
features: White functionalist stadium with a 72.71 m tower, the length of the 1932 Olympic javelin win.

photos.file: File:Helsinki Olympic Stadium in Taka-Töölö, Helsinki, Finland, 2026 July.jpg

note: Venue of the 1952 Olympics; reopened in 2020 after a renovation that added the dark timber canopy seen in recent photos. Photo 2 is from 1938.

name: Helsingborg Concert Hall
features: Classic Swedish functionalism: a tall white hall box fronted by a low curved foyer wing.
note: Designed from 1932, completed 1934 (Sven Markelius article). No English article of its own.

name: Kuokkala Church
by: Lassila Hirvilammi (Anssi Lassila, Teemu Hirvilammi, Jani Jansson)
features: A folded, slate-clad mass beside a slender slate bell tower, with a timber-ribbed nave inside.
note: No English Wikipedia article; facts from the Commons category description.

name: Lieksa Church
features: White glazed walls on a rough granite base under a low domed roof; a cross is drawn by the window mullions.
note: Facts from the Commons category description (designed by Raili and Reima Pietilä, completed 1982).

name: Lister County Courthouse
features: Ochre Nordic-classical courthouse with a clock gable and a great arched, fan-glazed entrance.

photos.file: File:Listers härads tingshus i Sölvesborg - 2024-08-20 - Bild 11.jpg
File:Listers härads tingshus i Sölvesborg - 2024-08-20 - Bild 10.jpg

note: Swedish name Listers härads tingshus. Built 1921 (Commons category), an early Asplund work in Nordic Classicism. No English Wikipedia article.

name: Löyly
features: Public sauna and restaurant under a faceted shell of timber slats that doubles as a climbable terrace.
note: Most files in the category are of people on the terraces; these three show the building.

name: Lund Konsthall
features: A plain brick wall on the square hides white galleries lit through tall sloping glass roofs.
note: No English Wikipedia article; architect and year from the Commons file descriptions ("Klas Anshelm 1957"). Good interior views of the top-lit halls are in the same category.

name: Sveriges Riksbank Building
features: Dark stone block of squares and cubes on Brunkebergstorg, composed to look solid and stable.
note: Headquarters of the Bank of Sweden. Wikipedia gives 1969–1973 for the design; the Commons category and a construction photo date completion to 1976.

name: St. Henry's Ecumenical Art Chapel
features: Copper-clad, boat-shaped chapel on a rocky ridge, with a pine-ribbed interior like an upturned hull.
commons_category: Category:Ecumenical Art Chapel of St. Henry

photos.file: File:Ecumenical Art Chapel of St. Henry out.jpg

note: No English Wikipedia article; architect and year from the Commons category (Churches by Matti Sanaksenaho; built 2005).

name: Akureyrarkirkja
features: Twin stepped towers of grooved concrete frame the entrance of a hilltop church above the fjord.
note: By the architect of Hallgrímskirkja (already on the wall); the stepped towers are often read as basalt columns.

name: Deichman Bjørvika (Oslo Public Library)
features: Glass-skinned library whose upper floors cantilever out toward the Opera, with an open, see-through ground floor.

photos.file: File:2020 wurde das neue Bibliotheksgebäude neben dem Opernhaus eröffnet. 02.jpg
File:2020 wurde das neue Bibliotheksgebäude neben dem Opernhaus eröffnet. 03.jpg
File:2020 wurde das neue Bibliotheksgebäude neben dem Opernhaus eröffnet. 04.jpg

note: Opened 18 June 2020, next to the Oslo Opera House.

name: Dokk1
by: Schmidt Hammer Lassen Architects, Kristine Jensen
features: Polygonal library and citizens' hall on a harbour pier: a glass box under a wide overhanging upper floor.

photos.file: File:Drone photo of Dokk1 in Aarhus, Denmark.jpg

name: Gothenburg Concert Hall
features: Functionalist hall on Götaplatsen: yellow brick with a tall glazed foyer front facing the square.
note: Wikipedia spells the architect Nils Einar Ericsson; the Commons category and the plaque on the building say Eriksson.

name: Gothenburg Law Courts Extension
features: A restrained new wing beside the old courthouse, around a top-lit, timber-lined atrium of stairs and galleries.
note: Only two exterior photos; the extension is famous for its interior, and Category:Göteborgs rådhusannexet has many good free photos of the atrium if interiors are wanted. Asplund worked on it 1913–1937.

name: Hornbækhus
features: A whole city block of brick flats, identical windows repeated without a break around one big green court.
note: Nordic Classicism; landscape architect G.N. Brandt (Commons). Wikipedia's Kay Fisker article gives 1922, Commons 1923. Photo 3 is a 1958 view of the courtyard.

name: Ørestad Gymnasium
features: A school without classrooms: open decks round an atrium joined by a broad winding stair, behind coloured louvres.
note: Only two exterior files (one is a facade close-up of the louvres); Commons has a CC0 interior of the atrium stair.

name: Ilulissat Icefjord Centre
features: A low, boomerang-shaped visitor centre at the edge of the icefjord, its sloping roof a walkway with a view.
note: Greenland (part of the Danish realm). Only one free photo, but a good one. Year is the opening year (2021); Wikipedia names the building but gives no date.

name: Nordic House in the Faroe Islands
features: A turf-roofed cultural centre like a hill of elves, its glass walls braced by steel struts against hurricane winds.
commons_category: Category:Nordic House in the Faroe Islands
note: Faroe Islands (FO). Won in a 1977 Nordic competition with 158 entries.

name: Powerhouse Brattørkaia
features: Energy-positive office: a dark wedge whose steep roof is one big solar array, cut by an oval courtyard.
note: Architect and year from the Commons category (Snøhetta; built 2019). Built to produce more energy than it uses over its life.

name: Reykjavík City Hall
features: Concrete blocks standing in Tjörnin lake on slender columns, around a public hall with a large relief map of Iceland.

photos.file: File:1992 wurde das Rathaus in Reykjavik eröffnet. 04.jpg
File:1992 wurde das Rathaus in Reykjavik eröffnet. 05.jpg
File:1992 wurde das Rathaus in Reykjavik eröffnet. 06.jpg

note: Built 1992 after an international competition won by Studio Granda.

name: SDU Campus Kolding
features: Triangular university building wrapped in perforated steel shutters that open and close with the daylight.
note: University of Southern Denmark. Facts from the Commons category (Henning Larsen Architects, 2012–2014).

name: St. Hallvard Church and Monastery
features: A square brick block outside, a round church within, under a concrete ceiling that sags down like a bowl.

photos.file: File:St. Hallvard kirke c1987–92 OMU OMu.D0626.jpg

note: Catholic church and Franciscan monastery on Enerhaugen. Commons files it under built 1962 and 1992; the church was consecrated in 1966. Photo 1 (c. 1987–92, from above) shows the bowl roof.

name: Stockholm Concert Hall
features: Blue Nordic-classical hall on Hötorget, fronted by a tall portico of slender columns over broad steps.

photos.file: File:Concert house steps are miles statue stockholm.jpg

note: Nordic Classicism; home of the Royal Stockholm Philharmonic and the Nobel Prize ceremony. Photo 3 is from 1965.

name: Tautra Mariakloster (convent)
features: Cistercian convent on a fjord island: slate-clad walls and lattice glass-and-timber roofs, near medieval ruins.
note: Commons mixes the new convent with the medieval abbey ruins in one category; the chosen photos show the new building. Architect from the Commons file descriptions; 2006 is when the community became autonomous (Wikipedia) and the usual completion date.

name: The Twist
features: Gallery, bridge and sculpture in one: an aluminium-clad box that turns 90° as it spans 60 m over the river.
note: At the Kistefos Museum; opened 18 September 2019 (Commons).

name: Under
features: A concrete tube sunk into the sea off the rocks, its dining room 5.5 m down behind one wide window.
note: Only one exterior photo; the rest of the category shows the dining room and food. Opened in 2019.

name: Wadden Sea Centre
features: Low visitor centre on the marsh whose thatch runs over the roof and down the walls, in long sloping planes.

photos.file: File:20191010 Vadehavscentret pa Jylland ritat av Dorte Mandrup003 (48965849311).jpg
File:20191010 Vadehavscentret pa Jylland ritat av Dorte Mandrup012-2 (48965858781).jpg

note: Near Ribe. Mandrup's rebuild won Building of the Year 2017 (Wikipedia); the category also holds the older centre, avoid File:2013-07 Vadehavscenteret before the reconstruction.jpg.

name: Kela Main Office (National Pensions Institute)
features: Red-brick and copper office block stepped round a raised courtyard, with a top-lit main hall inside.
note: Completed 1956 (Commons; Wikipedia list gives 1953–1956).

name: KTH School of Architecture
features: Round-cornered studio building clad in rust-brown metal, its wide windows bending with the curved walls.
note: Built 2013–2015 at Osquars backe 9 (Commons file descriptions); Kasper Salin Prize. No English Wikipedia article on the building.
